reference.title: Starfish Crunch (beginner) (male)
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl and turn, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up and turn, a short squeeze, about 1.4 s down, then switch sides

prescription.tempo: About 1 s up and reach, brief touch, 1.5 s down
prescription.progression: Lift the leg straight to meet the hand (full starfish crunch), then both arms and legs together

cues.text: Lie in a star: legs straight and apart, arms overhead in a wide V, all resting on the mat.
Breathe out, curl up and turn, reaching the right hand across to the left shin as the left knee bends in.
Breathe in and lower back to the star, arm and leg long again.
Repeat to the other side: left hand to the right shin.
Lower with control and keep alternating.

mistakes.fix: Curl and turn the trunk first; the arm follows.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the knee all the way to the chest to meet the hand
mistakes.fix: Draw the knee in only part way; make the trunk do the work.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching as the leg returns
mistakes.fix: Brace and lower the leg slowly.
Look toward the knee, chin slightly tucked.

kinematics.measure: Upper trunk (T12 to C7) from the floor
kinematics.norm: Shoulder blades clear the mat as in a crunch (clinical opinion)
Upper trunk turns toward the opposite knee; twisting curl-ups raise external oblique activity (Konrad 2001)
Beginner: the knee bends and draws in (the advanced form lifts the straight leg) (clinical opinion)
One hand reaches across to the opposite shin; the other rests overhead (clinical opinion)
Controlled, a short pause at the reach (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.

Low-back pain, disc problems or flexion intolerance: start with a McGill-style curl-up, dead bug or plank; partial curl-ups gave the best abdominal challenge for the least spine compression in one model study (Axler and McGill 1997).
Combined flexion and twisting under fatigue is a common trigger of back pain; keep the reps controlled and stop the set when form slips (clinical opinion).
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before dynamic trunk-flexion work.
Osteoporosis or vertebral fracture: avoid repeated loaded spinal flexion and twisting.
The athlete mesh rests on the mat; the rig collision shapes are thicker than the mesh at the back and buttocks, so floorTolerance records how far those proxy shapes sink below the mat surface.
modify: Neck pain: cross the arms on the chest and turn the chest.
regressions: Keep both legs on the mat and reach to the opposite knee.
Twisting crunch with the feet flat.
progressions: Slower lowering with a 2 s touch.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the trunk up to the reach (about 56% MVC in a cross curl-up, Konrad 2001).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: External oblique on the reaching side and internal oblique on the other side turn the trunk toward the knee (Konrad 2001; Crommert 2021).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: External oblique on the reaching side and internal oblique on the other side turn the trunk toward the knee (Konrad 2001; Crommert 2021).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Draw the knee in on the first side (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Draw the knee in on the second side (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Reaches the shoulder blade forward with the hand (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Reaches the shoulder blade forward with the hand (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the resting leg long (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the resting leg long (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Right hand reaches to the left shin
